newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares end steady, prices seen holding.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares end steady, prices seen holding.

text.p: Russian shares held steady on Wednesday after a correction which set in last Friday and dealers said prices were likely to remain around the same levels over the next few weeks rather than resume the sharp growth of earlier this year.
The 23-share Russian Trading System index ended unchanged from Tuesday's close at 327.35, edging down from modest gains earlier, on total market volume of $28.71 million.
"Only Megionneftegaz dropped noticably today," said Samit Yakovlev, senior trader at United City Bank. "In the end we found the market was supported."
Megionneftegaz closed at $6.20, down from $6.60 at Tuesday's close on publication of a fall in crude oil output in 1996, Andrei Kukk, head of the trading department Rinako Plus.

Gazprom, the day's most heavily traded share, rose to $0.571 from $0.540. Surgutneftegaz rose to $0.775 from $0.750 after a pension fund in the Surgut group won a 40 percent stake in Surgutneftegaz's main shareholder, Surgut Holding.
Rinako's Kukk said the market was not likely to grow or fall sharply in the near future.

"The market is tired. If it moves, it will be even and slow, because every big buy is accompanied by a big sale," he said. "The market will hang at these levels for a month or two, with maximum growth or decline of five percent."
He added some shares may get a second wind after a series of shareholder meetings scheduled over the next few months.
"When the shareholders' meetings are over, investors will see what position the company is in," Kukk said.

"If the published results spur investors to buy, there will be a wave of growth. If results are such that investors think it is time to get out of the stock, then there will be a fall in individual shares but nothing catastrophic," he said.
